output.brief: FCR fell because of the Finance change on 14 April, not mainly because of the new starters. That change cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred there jumped from 7% to 54% in the same week FCR dropped. Referred calls resolve at about 33%, and non-referred calls are unchanged at 82%. Referral rates are the same across tenure bands, and tenured agents' FCR fell as much as the April intake's. That points away from inexperience. Tariff mix and the IVR redesign show little effect: tariff calls still resolve at 85%, and the drop came before the IVR change on 28 April. Workload is unestablished. Complaints rose, but their link to FCR is unproven. Next step: agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Add post-call sampling, and track FCR and unsupported credits. Do not put the April starters on performance plans, because it would punish the wrong group. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. I'm fairly confident in the main finding. Workload and IVR remain open.
